concept_options.title: The box shuts behind you
concept_options.hook: You walk into the kitchen with no idea why. The door did that.
concept_options.visual_approach: Black ink on white paper. A hand-drawn figure sketches itself into existence, then carries a small orange errand across the frame. The doorway it walks through is a contraption: a frame with a lid-arm that swipes the errand off as the figure crosses, drops it in a box, stamps the lid shut and slides the box onto a growing stack of identical closed boxes. The figure arrives empty-handed and wanders. It walks back through the door — the box stays shut, and that is the beat the whole piece turns on. It ends pulled back on the stack, every box a finished room. Every movement of the figure is real motion capture; nothing about the acting is hand-tuned.
concept_options.target_audience: Everyone. This is the one topic where the viewer has already run the experiment on themselves this week.
key_points: You walk into a room and the reason is gone — universally recognised, mildly humiliating
It is not age and not decline; it happens to healthy people at every age
The experiment: same distance, across a room versus through a doorway; the doorway one is worse
A room is treated as one finished event; crossing the threshold closes it and files it
The remedy everyone has been given — go back to where you were — was tested and did not work
It mostly only catches you when your head was already full
Splitting into events costs you the errand and buys you the understanding
concept_options.core_message: The forgetting is not a fault in the machine, it is the sound the machine makes when it finishes a room — and the advice you were given about going back does not work.
concept_options.tone: Deadpan, warm, faintly slapstick. The character is never cute and never mugs; the comedy is that it keeps doing a reasonable thing and the door keeps taking its errand.
grounded_in: underserved_gap: nobody has staged this as an action, and it is entirely an action
underserved_gap: the folk remedy was tested and failed
underserved_gap: the effect is load-dependent, not universal
data_point: surface memory worse, mental model better
concept_options.why_this_works: The topic is the most saturated the channel has touched — dozens of shorts run the same script — so the differentiation has to come from two places at once, and this concept has both. The content differentiation is the three findings the corpus omits, in the order that makes them land. The form differentiation is that the mechanism here is literally a person carrying something across a threshold, so for the first time this channel can act the idea out instead of diagramming it, and a doodle losing its errand to a door is funny in a way no chart has ever been.

concept_options.title: It only gets you when your arms are full
concept_options.hook: The door isn't taking things from you. It's just where you drop them.
concept_options.visual_approach: The figure staggers under a swaying tower of objects. Doorway after doorway; each crossing knocks the top item off. When it carries one thing, the doorway takes nothing.
concept_options.target_audience: General, skewing toward people who feel scattered
key_points: Four experiments in 2021 found no reliable doorway effect
So the doorway is where an overloaded head drops something
The fix is not the doorway, it is the load
concept_options.core_message: Doorways don't erase things. Overloaded heads do, and the doorway is only where it shows.
grounded_in: 2021 multimodal study: no significant effect except under working-memory load
concept_options.why_this_works: The most honest framing in the literature, the most actionable, and visually the funniest single image in the whole set — a doodle under a swaying tower. Its weakness is that it opens by deflating the phenomenon before the viewer has been allowed to enjoy it, and a myth-bust needs a myth the audience currently holds; here the audience holds the *experience*, not a belief. Its payload becomes the qualifier late in c-boxes.

concept_options.title: They actually ran this
concept_options.hook: Somebody put this in a lab. Two tables, one door, and a box you can't look in.
concept_options.visual_approach: The figure re-enacts the real protocol as a diagram that it walks through: table, object into a box, cross the room or cross the doorway, get probed. A tally builds beside each condition.
concept_options.target_audience: Viewers who like knowing how a claim was actually established
key_points: Objects concealed in boxes so vision cannot help
The distance is held constant; only the doorway varies
Virtual first, then a real building, same result
Then the third condition: back through two doorways to the start
concept_options.core_message: The finding is not folklore; it is a controlled comparison with the distance held constant.
grounded_in: Same distance across a room versus through a doorway
concept_options.why_this_works: The most rigorous, and it would satisfy anyone who suspects pop psychology. But re-enacting a protocol spends the running time on method rather than on the thing the viewer feels, and it turns the character into a lab subject rather than a person — which throws away the one advantage of having a character at all. Its best beat, the return condition, is the turn in c-boxes.

concept_options.title: An argument with a door
concept_options.visual_approach: Two characters: the figure and the doorway itself, which answers in speech balloons. The figure accuses; the door explains itself; the figure concedes.
key_points: The door did it on purpose
The door is doing its job
concept_options.core_message: The thing that lost your errand is the thing that lets you think.
grounded_in: Event segmentation as a feature rather than a fault
Surface memory worse, mental model better
concept_options.why_this_works: The funniest, and InkTheater.balloon exists precisely for it. But dialogue between a figure and a door means the video is carried by written jokes rather than by the mechanism, the reading load on a phone doubles, and a talking door is a bigger swing than a first character piece should take. One balloon survives into c-boxes.

selected_concept.rationale: It is the only one of the four in which the character is doing the thing the video is about, rather than demonstrating it, arguing about it or being a subject in it. The mechanism — carrying something across a threshold and losing it — is physical acting, and physical acting is the register this channel has never used and the style ledger now requires. It also carries all three of the findings the saturated corpus omits, and it holds the strongest of them, the failed return, as its turn rather than as an aside.
modifications: Absorb c-load's payload as the late qualifier, so the video does not overstate the effect the way every other treatment does
Absorb c-restage's return condition as the turn — but staged as the character walking back, not as a protocol diagram
Keep exactly one speech balloon from c-argument, at the moment the character arrives empty-handed, and let it be the only written joke in the piece
One character, not two. The doorway is a contraption, not a co-star; giving it a voice would double the reading load.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: The mocap library has twelve clips and none of them is 'stands still and looks around, confused' — which is the single most important beat in the video.
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Use `shuffle` (a slow sneaking creep) for the wandering, which reads exactly as aimless searching, and carry the confusion in the staging — the empty hands, the balloon, the stillness — rather than in a pose. If it does not read, extend the library with ink-theater/mocap/add-motion.mjs, which pulls free CMU motion through GitHub and is reachable from here.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: InkPuppet keeps the figure horizontally fixed at cx and only moves it vertically, so a walk clip walks on the spot.
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Move the world instead of the character: the room, the doorway and the boxes live in a group that slides past a fixed figure. This is the classic side-scroller solution, it is deterministic, and it puts the doorway's arrival under exact timeline control — which matters because the swipe has to land on a specific word.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Piper is a small local neural voice and remains the weakest component across all four productions.
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Ship on Piper. A cloud TTS key is still the single largest available quality upgrade, and still declined under the standing 'nothing paid' constraint.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: The topic is genuinely saturated — dozens of near-identical shorts exist.
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Accept it, because the differentiation is real and double: three findings the corpus omits, and a form nobody has used on it. But say so honestly in the ledger rather than pretending the field was empty.

alternative_paths.description: Remotion atelier again, hand-drawing the figure and animating it by hand
alternative_paths.what_changes: A fourth production on a runtime used by two of the previous three, with hand-tuned character motion that the ink-sketch style explicitly forbids. Rejected on both counts.

alternative_paths.description: Manim again, diagramming the effect as boxes and arrows
alternative_paths.what_changes: Would work and would look good, and the style ledger forbids it outright for this production. It is also the wrong register for a topic the user asked to be understandable by everyone.

alternative_paths.description: The same edit with a cloud TTS voice
alternative_paths.what_changes: Materially better narration across the whole channel. Blocked by the standing constraint; recorded so it stays visible.

production_plan.art_direction: Black ink on warm white paper (#FCFBF8), the ink-sketch playbook. All structure and the character are ink #333 with a live hand-drawn boil on every stroke. The colour grammar is the style's own, mapped to this story: orange #E8722C is the errand and only the errand — it is the thing that flows through the piece and the only warm mark on the page; red #C8322B appears once, on the lid of the box that will not open; blue #2E6E9E appears once, at the close, on the stack that turns out to be the point. Type is Patrick Hand, the full TTF, on HTML overlay divs — the first handwriting this channel has used. The signature device is the doorway itself, drawn as a contraption: an upright frame with a hinged lid-arm that swipes across as the figure crosses, and a box that stamps shut under it. Motion character is the largest departure of all four productions: real human motion capture. The figure walks, creeps and sits like a person because a person did it; nothing about the acting is authored. The world slides past a fixed figure, so the camera language is a single horizontal scroll rather than cuts — the whole piece is one continuous shot with the doorway arriving and leaving.

taste_profile.design_read: A doodle on a sheet of paper is trying to run an errand, and the paper keeps taking it away.
taste_profile.palette_discipline: Ink on white, plus three marks. Orange is the errand and nothing else. Red appears exactly once, on the shut lid. Blue appears exactly once, on the closing stack. If any of the three shows up anywhere else in the render, that is a defect.
taste_profile.layout_variation: One continuous horizontal scroll rather than a cut list: room, doorway, room, back through the doorway, then a pull-back onto the stack. The variation is in what enters the frame, not in how the frame is divided — which is the opposite of the previous three productions and is the point.
taste_profile.reference_strategy: Grammar only, from productions/references/wpmavi-power-lines: name the current idea on screen, caption the words with the load-bearing word marked, one accent plus one reserved colour. The reference's cut-every-four-seconds rule is deliberately broken here — this piece is one shot, because the joke needs continuity to work.
anti_patterns: Hand-tuned character motion of any kind — sine curves, hand-posed keyframes, an eased limb. Forbidden by the style and by this plan.
A cute mascot. Deadpan or nothing.
Looping one mocap clip for the whole video — the skill names this as what makes character work feel repetitive
Any grid, ruler, caliper, chart or measured number — that is the previous production and it must not leak in
Any dark ground, glow or instrument framing — that is the two before it
Explaining with the words 'event boundary', 'event segmentation' or 'event horizon model'. The mechanism is described in furniture.
quality_gates: Every character movement traces to a named clip in ink-theater/mocap/catalog.json; no clip is used twice in a row
Orange appears only on the errand; red once; blue once
The handwriting renders as handwriting, verified on a snapshot — the font-subset trap makes this fail silently
hyperframes lint clean before every render
Reviewed against all three STYLE_LEDGER rows on all five fields before render

music_source.mood_direction: Silence under the narration, and three locally synthesised sounds only: a pencil scratch as the figure draws itself in, a wooden clack as the lid stamps shut, and nothing at all under the closing pull-back. Produced with ffmpeg synthesis; no library, no provider, no key.

voice_selection.rationale: The only TTS available offline here. Measured at 3.2 words per second across the previous productions.
voice_selection.delivery_style: Warm and dry, closer to a friend telling you something than to a narrator. This is the first production where the voice should sound amused; the three before it were all deliberately level.
voice_selection.pacing_policy: Synthesise per section, measure each real duration, and cut the animation to those measurements. Never estimate.

line_items.notes: Local Chromium; the smoke test rendered 4s in 18s wall clock

line_items.operation: Narration synthesis, one wav per script section
Pre-baked motion clips, chosen by name
line_items.notes: Ships with the repository; CMU mocap is free for any use

line_items.operation: Sound synthesis, audio mux, -14 LUFS, faststart

savings_options: Already at zero. The only paid option anywhere in the plan is a cloud TTS voice, declined under the standing constraint.

approval.user_notes: Standing pre-authorisation, restated by the user for this production: pick a topic everyone can understand and build it using OpenMontage's full capability set, no questions. The constraints attached remain: vertical short, original script, natural fluent English narration, burned captions, royalty-free or self-produced audio, nothing paid for. Recorded here rather than as a decision_log entry because the decision_log schema's category enum still has no 'approval_policy' value even though AGENT_GUIDE.md requires that category for full-run pre-authorisation — the same schema/guide disagreement flagged on all three previous productions.

metadata.rig_complexity: low — one six-part hand-drawn figure (head, spine, two arms, two legs) posed from baked motion-capture frames. No per-character code path; the character is data.
metadata.reuse_strategy: One rig, one draw-in reveal, and named clips from the shared mocap catalog. Every prop in the piece is parametric ink from the InkTheater primitives rather than authored art, so nothing has to be drawn twice and nothing is generated.
metadata.sample_first_plan: A four-second vertical smoke build was rendered before any production work: the figure draws itself in, walks on real mocap, the boil filter runs and the handwriting font resolves — all at 1080x1920, 120 frames, 18 seconds wall clock. This de-risked the three things most likely to fail (vertical output, a blocked gsap CDN, and the silent font-subset fallback) before a line of the real composition was written.
metadata.world_rotation_check: STYLE_LEDGER.md records Remotion atelier for productions 1 and 2, Manim for production 3, and states plainly that production 4 may not use Manim. Ink Theater plus Ink Puppet is untouched. This is also the first production not composited in Remotion at all.
metadata.ledger_overlap_check: Checked against all three rows on all five fields. Design read: new — the previous three were an oscilloscope, a corrected physics plate and a machine shop; this is a doodle on a sheet of paper. Ground: new — warm white paper with no grain and no border, against #080B10, #EDE6D6 with grain and a plate border, and #161A26. Palette roles: new — ink plus orange/red/blue, none of which has appeared. Signature device: new — a doorway with a lid-arm, against a running counter, three unequal arrows and a caliper. Layout set: new, and structurally new — one continuous horizontal scroll instead of a cut list. Motion character: the largest departure in the channel's history — real human motion capture, against constant-velocity flight, spring overshoot and mechanical stepping. No warnings to record on this one.

decisions.subject: Pipeline for a character-led vertical explainer

options_considered.label: character-animation
options_considered.reason: The subject is a person carrying something across a threshold. That is acting, and this is the only pipeline whose stages are character design, rig plan, pose library and action timeline.

options_considered.label: animated-explainer
options_considered.reason: Carried the three previous productions and is fully understood.
options_considered.rejected_because: Its stages assume the visual is composed rather than performed. It has no character_design or rig_plan stage, which is exactly where the work is here.

options_considered.label: animation
options_considered.reason: Motion-graphics-first, and the ink-sketch style runs on it for illustration pieces.
options_considered.rejected_because: skills/creative/ink-theater.md routes a mocap character to character-animation and an illustration or contraption piece to animation. This has a mocap character.

decisions.reason: The pipeline whose contract matches the work. It is also beta, which is worth saying out loud: expect rough edges in its tooling and be ready to hand-author an artifact against the schema if a stage tool disagrees with it.

decisions.subject: Angle and staging for the doorway-effect short

options_considered.label: The box shuts behind you
options_considered.reason: The only concept where the character does the thing the video is about rather than demonstrating it. Carries all three omitted findings and holds the strongest one — the failed return — as the turn.

options_considered.label: It only gets you when your arms are full
options_considered.reason: The most honest framing in the literature and the funniest single image in the set.
options_considered.rejected_because: It deflates the phenomenon before the viewer has been allowed to enjoy it, and a myth-bust needs a belief to bust; the audience holds an experience, not a belief. Absorbed as the late qualifier.

options_considered.label: They actually ran this
options_considered.reason: The most rigorous, and it would satisfy anyone who suspects pop psychology.
options_considered.rejected_because: Spends the runtime on method rather than on the thing the viewer feels, and turns the character into a lab subject — which throws away the only reason to have a character. Its best beat became the turn.

options_considered.label: An argument with a door
options_considered.reason: The funniest, and InkTheater.balloon exists precisely for it.
options_considered.rejected_because: Dialogue would carry the video instead of the mechanism, and it doubles the reading load on a phone. One balloon survives.

decisions.reason: The mechanism is physical and so is the concept. The other three each contributed one thing: the load qualifier, the return condition, and a single speech balloon.

decisions.subject: Drawn world for this production, under the manifesto's rotation rule

options_considered.label: Ink Theater + Ink Puppet (ink-sketch playbook)
options_considered.reason: Unused. It is also the only world on the manifesto's table whose native subject is a character performing an action, which is what this topic is made of, and its register — a doodle on paper — is the most immediately readable thing available for a topic the user asked to be understandable by everyone.

options_considered.label: Manim
options_considered.reason: Carried the previous production and worked well.
options_considered.rejected_because: STYLE_LEDGER.md states in writing that production 4 may not use Manim. It is also the wrong register for this brief.

options_considered.label: Remotion atelier vector composition
options_considered.reason: Carried productions 1 and 2; fully understood.
options_considered.rejected_because: Two of the last three. And hand-authoring a walk cycle in it would be hand-tuned character motion, which the ink-sketch style forbids outright.

options_considered.label: HyperFrames kinetic typography
options_considered.reason: Unused as a *style*, and strong when the words are the visual.
options_considered.rejected_because: Here the words are not the visual; a person losing something is. The runtime is used, the style is not — held for a future production where the type is the subject.

options_considered.label: threejs_world
options_considered.reason: Unused, and a doorway is genuinely spatial.
options_considered.rejected_because: A 3D room would make the piece about the room. The point is that the room is a container, not a place, and a flat doodle says that better than a rendered space.

decisions.reason: Rotation requires a new world, the topic requires acting, and this is the only world that does acting. Its character motion is real motion capture, which also makes it the largest single change to this channel's motion language so far.

decisions.subject: Composition runtime for the final assembly

options_considered.label: HyperFrames 0.8.29 (available: true)
options_considered.reason: The runtime the ink-sketch style is built for: HTML/SVG/CSS driven by one paused GSAP timeline, rendered to MP4. It also ships lint, validate, snapshot and inspect, which give this production a review loop the previous three had to improvise. A vertical 1080x1920 smoke build rendered in 18 seconds wall clock before this decision was taken.

options_considered.label: Remotion (available: true)
options_considered.reason: Carried all three previous productions and is completely understood here.
options_considered.rejected_because: Ink Theater and Ink Puppet are written against HyperFrames' contract — one paused timeline, seek-safe determinism. Porting them to Remotion would mean rewriting the engine to use it, which is the opposite of reusing engine knowledge.

options_considered.label: FFmpeg (available: true)
options_considered.reason: Always available, and it will still do the audio mux and the loudness pass.
options_considered.rejected_because: It cannot render a browser composition. Retained for exactly the job it is right for: muxing the narration and normalising to -14 LUFS.

decisions.reason: All three runtimes are available on this machine and all three were evaluated, as the hard rule requires. HyperFrames is chosen because the style's engine is written for its contract. If it became unavailable at compose time that is a blocker to escalate, not a silent swap.

decisions.subject: How the character's movement is authored

options_considered.label: Real CMU motion capture via InkPuppet.choreograph
options_considered.reason: The agent chooses named clips and nothing else. Motion looks human because a human did it, and it is deterministic and seek-safe because each pose is a pure function of the segment's local time.

options_considered.label: Hand-authored limb curves
options_considered.reason: Total control.
options_considered.rejected_because: Explicitly forbidden by skills/creative/ink-theater.md — 'never hand-tune character motion' — and it is forbidden for a good reason: hand-tuned walk cycles are the tell that separates a doodle that moves from a doodle that is alive.

decisions.reason: The style's rule, and the whole reason the character world is worth using. Clips are picked per beat from mocap/catalog.json and no clip is used twice in a row.

decisions.subject: Authoring mode

options_considered.label: Atelier — hand-authored composition on the engine primitives
options_considered.reason: Consistent with the three previous productions and with the manifesto. The engine supplies strokes, boil, springs and the puppet; every scene, prop and beat in this piece is written for it alone.

options_considered.label: HyperFrames registry blocks
options_considered.reason: Fast and reliable.
options_considered.rejected_because: Registry blocks are frozen looks. The atelier doctrine puts them off-limits for hero work, and this channel exists because five templated videos looked identical.

decisions.reason: Engine knowledge is reused; creative components are not.

decisions.subject: Style playbook

options_considered.label: ink-sketch (Ink Theater)
options_considered.reason: Hand-drawn ink-on-white doodle animation with a character that draws itself and acts the idea out. It is the playbook this concept is made of.

options_considered.label: flat-motion-graphics
options_considered.reason: The pipeline manifest's recommended playbook for character-animation.
options_considered.rejected_because: The manifest recommends it; a recommendation is input, not a decision. Its bounce and colour would fight motion capture, which is quiet and human rather than snappy.

options_considered.label: minimalist-diagram
options_considered.reason: Carried the previous production well.
options_considered.rejected_because: That is the previous production, and the user asked for something everyone can understand rather than something precise.

decisions.reason: The playbook and the concept are the same object. Its strict colour grammar is adopted and mapped to this story explicitly in the art direction.

decisions.subject: Narration TTS provider

options_considered.label: Piper en_US-ryan-high (local)
options_considered.reason: The only TTS configured here. Fluent, correctly stressed, free, offline, and measured at about 3.2 words per second across the previous productions.

options_considered.label: A cloud voice (ElevenLabs, Azure or Gemini)
options_considered.reason: Materially better, and this is the production that would benefit most — it is the first script with any warmth in it, and Piper is level by nature.
options_considered.rejected_because: No key is configured and the standing constraint is that nothing is paid for until the channel earns. Recorded again so the option stays visible; it is now the fourth production to name it.

decisions.reason: Availability and the zero-cost constraint. Named in the quality tradeoffs as the weakest component.

decisions.subject: Music and sound

options_considered.label: Silence plus three self-produced sounds
options_considered.reason: A pencil scratch while the figure draws itself, a wooden clack when the lid stamps shut, and nothing under the close. Each one marks a physical event, which is what a piece about physical acting needs.

options_considered.label: A generated background track
options_considered.reason: Available in principle through music_generation.
options_considered.rejected_because: 0 of 5 music_generation providers are configured on this machine, and a bed would flatten three sounds that are meant to be the only things you hear.

options_considered.label: A track from music_library/
options_considered.reason: The drop path exists.
options_considered.rejected_because: music_library/ is empty; the capability reports 0 of 1 configured.

decisions.reason: Silence is the design. The three sounds are synthesised locally with ffmpeg, so nothing is licensed and nothing is fetched.

decisions.subject: Source of the visual material — drawn versus photographed

options_considered.label: Every frame drawn, per productions/MANIFESTO.md
options_considered.reason: The channel's position, and here it is also the only workable choice: the only thing a camera can show is a person looking puzzled in a kitchen, which is a picture of the symptom.

options_considered.label: Stock footage of a person in a doorway
options_considered.reason: It is what every other treatment uses.
options_considered.rejected_because: Two reasons and the second is the real one. This environment's network policy denies every media host tested — thirteen of them, recorded in productions/ENVIRONMENT.md. Editorially, a photograph of a doorway contains no boxes, no lid and no stack, so the annotation would have nothing to point at.

decisions.reason: The manifesto, and the fact that the mechanism has no photograph.

decisions.subject: Whether to extend the mocap action library for this piece

options_considered.label: Use only the twelve clips already in mocap/catalog.json
options_considered.reason: No new dependency, no fetch, no conversion step. `shuffle` — a slow sneaking creep — reads convincingly as aimless searching, which is the beat that matters most.

options_considered.label: Add clips with ink-theater/mocap/add-motion.mjs
options_considered.reason: The script pulls free CMU motion through GitHub, which is on this environment's allowlist, and auto-maps the skeleton. A dedicated 'look around, confused' clip would be better than shuffle for the central beat.

decisions.reason: Start with what ships and let the snapshot review decide. If the wandering beat does not read as confusion on the contact sheet, extend then — the option is live and the host is reachable, so this is a deferral rather than a rejection.
